status_note: Reproduces on Spark 4.3.0 (and 4.0.1); main not read. The javadoc of `CollationAwareUTF8String.toUpperCase(UTF8String)` and `toLowerCase(UTF8String)` says "using the ICU root locale rules"; the code calls `UCharacter.toUpperCase(String)`, which takes the JVM's default locale. No upstream issue searched yet.
title: `upper` and `lower` of a UTF8_BINARY string follow the JVM's default locale
summary: With `spark.sql.icu.caseMappings.enabled` (the default) `upper` and `lower` of a non-ASCII `UTF8_BINARY` string go through `CollationAwareUTF8String.toUpperCase(UTF8String)`, documented as "using the ICU root locale rules", and call `UCharacter.toUpperCase(String)` and `toLowerCase(String)`, ICU's default-locale overloads. Under a JVM whose default locale is Turkish or Azeri, `lower('Ié')` is `ıé` and `upper('iÉ')` is `İÉ`; under Lithuanian `lower('Ì')` keeps a dot above. Executors have JVMs of their own, so the same query maps by each executor's locale. A fully ASCII string takes a byte path and is unaffected.
repro: Start the JVM with `-Duser.language=tr`: `SELECT lower('Ié'), upper('iÉ');` gives `ıé`, `İÉ`; with `-Duser.language=en` it gives `ié`, `IÉ`. `SELECT lower(collate('Ié', 'UNICODE'))` gives `ié` under both.
handling: Spark's writer emits `collate(upper(collate(x, 'UNICODE')), 'UTF8_BINARY')` (and `lower`) on text not proved ASCII (D51, `spark-case-collated`), which takes the collation's locale. The fix upstream is to pass `ULocale.ROOT` as the javadoc says.

checked.note: https://github.com/apache/spark/blob/v4.3.0/common/unsafe/src/main/java/org/apache/spark/sql/catalyst/util/CollationAwareUTF8String.java#L392-L443 (javadoc at L392, `UCharacter.toUpperCase(target.toValidString())` at L406); probes in engines/spark/probes/case-tables-settings.json (JVM locales tr, az, lt)
